decisions.reason: It is a higher-value analytical extension of the firm’s core pricing and market-data platform and, having survived the 2024 portfolio pruning, now looks like a strategically anchored module rather than a withdrawal candidate.

This gas tariff comparison tool is very close to the firm’s established utility-market business, and after the withdrawal of a broader comparison line it appears to be the more focused and commercially relevant offer to retain.

Although it still carries some overlap risk as a tariff-calculation product line and was less prominently presented than others, it likely remains the firm’s preferred broader calculator family after weaker adjacent products were removed.
As an enabling area-definition component for several location-based products and a good fit with the central-platform strategy, it is more likely to be retained as infrastructure than dropped.
